preamble.summary: Proverbs 6 treats four distinct-topics in sequence: (1) warnings-against-becoming-surety (vv. 1–5), (2) the-ant-as-model-of-wisdom (vv. 6–11), (3) the seven-things-the-LORD-hates catalog (vv. 16–19), and (4) the second-adulteress-warning (vv. 20–35). The seven-abominations list is the Hebrew Bible's most-focused catalog of divine-hatreds.
preamble.notable_variants: 6:6 'go to the ant, O sluggard' classical wisdom-observation; 6:16–19 'six things the LORD hates, seven are an abomination to him' — the divine-hatred catalog; 6:20–35 second adulteress-warning with reputation-destruction emphasis.

variant_notes: 'My son, if you have put up security for your neighbor, have given your pledge for a stranger' tracks MT. SURETY WARNING begins. Proverbs 11:15, 17:18, 20:16, 22:26, 27:13 share the strong warnings against surety.
'If you are snared in the words of your mouth, caught in the words of your mouth' tracks MT.
'Then do this, my son, and save yourself, for you have come into the hand of your neighbor: go, hasten, and plead urgently with your neighbor' tracks MT.
'Give your eyes no sleep and your eyelids no slumber' tracks MT.
'Save yourself like a gazelle from the hand of the hunter, like a bird from the hand of the fowler' tracks MT. GAZELLE-FROM-HAND / BIRD-FROM-FOWLER — the escape imagery. Ps 124:7 echoes.

'Go to the ant, O sluggard; consider her ways, and be wise' tracks MT. ANT-TO-SLUGGARD observation. The LXX adds a significant-plus in some textual-traditions: additional wisdom-sayings about the ant and about the bee. The bee-plus (absent from MT and most English translations) reads roughly: 'Or go to the bee, and learn how diligent she is … her work kings and commoners use for health.'
'Without having any chief, officer, or ruler' tracks MT. ANT-SELF-MOTIVATED — without-supervisor organization.
'She prepares her bread in summer and gathers her food in harvest' tracks MT.
'How long will you lie there, O sluggard? When will you arise from your sleep?' tracks MT.
'A little sleep, a little slumber, a little folding of the hands to rest' tracks MT. THE SLUGGARD'S MOTTO — repeated at Prov 24:33.
'And poverty will come upon you like a robber, and want like an armed man' tracks MT.

'A worthless person, a wicked man, goes about with crooked speech' tracks MT. 'WORTHLESS PERSON' (adam beliyaal / anēr aphrōn). Beliyaal — the 'worthless-one' — became a demonic title in Second-Temple and NT literature. 2 Corinthians 6:15 ('what accord has Christ with BELIAR?') uses the Hebrew-Aramaic form.
'Winks with his eyes, signals with his feet, points with his finger' tracks MT. SECRET-SIGNALING deceivers.
'With perverted heart devises evil, continually sowing discord' tracks MT. SOW-DISCORD — anti-community.
'Therefore calamity will come upon him suddenly; in a moment he will be broken beyond healing' tracks MT.

'There are six things that the LORD hates, seven that are an abomination to him' tracks MT. SIX-SEVEN WISDOM-FORMULA — common Hebrew numerical-parallelism (cf. Prov 30:15–31, Job 5:19, Amos 1–2). The 'seven' is climactic.
'Haughty eyes, a lying tongue, and hands that shed innocent blood' tracks MT. FIRST-THREE of the seven.
'A heart that devises wicked plans, feet that make haste to run to evil' tracks MT. FOURTH-AND-FIFTH. The 'feet swift to run to evil' vocabulary-family reappears in Rom 3:15 catena.

'A false witness who breathes out lies, and one who sows discord among brothers' tracks MT. SIXTH-AND-SEVENTH (the climactic seventh): DISCORD-SOWING between brothers. The SEVENTH-hated-thing is relationship-poisoning — God's highest-listed abomination concerning human-relations.
'My son, keep your father's commandment, and forsake not your mother's teaching' tracks MT. // Prov 1:8. The adulteress-warning resumes.
'Bind them on your heart always; tie them around your neck' tracks MT.
'When you walk, they will lead you; when you lie down, they will watch over you; and when you awake, they will talk with you' tracks MT. 24/7-INSTRUCTION — wisdom's companion-role.
'For the commandment is a lamp and the teaching a light, and the reproofs of discipline are the way of life' tracks MT. COMMANDMENT-IS-LAMP // Ps 119:105's 'your word is a lamp.'
'To preserve you from the evil woman, from the smooth tongue of the adulteress' tracks MT.

'Do not desire her beauty in your heart, and do not let her capture you with her eyelashes' tracks MT. HEART-DESIRE warning. Matthew 5:28 ('whoever looks at a woman with lustful intent has already committed adultery with her in his heart') directly extends.
'For the price of a prostitute is only a loaf of bread, but a married woman hunts down a precious life' tracks MT.
'Can a man carry fire next to his chest and his clothes not be burned?' tracks MT. FIRE-NEXT-TO-CHEST proverb — rhetorical impossibility of adultery-without-damage.
'Or can one walk on hot coals and his feet not be scorched?' tracks MT.
'So is he who goes in to his neighbor's wife; none who touches her will go unpunished' tracks MT.
'People do not despise a thief if he steals to satisfy his appetite when he is hungry' tracks MT.
'But if he is caught, he will pay sevenfold; he will give all the goods of his house' tracks MT. SEVENFOLD-RESTITUTION — theft punishment (Exodus 22:1's five/fourfold, Prov 6:31's sevenfold).
'He who commits adultery lacks sense; he who does it destroys himself' tracks MT.
'He will get wounds and dishonor, and his disgrace will not be wiped away' tracks MT.
'For jealousy makes a man furious, and he will not spare when he takes revenge' tracks MT.
'He will accept no compensation; he will refuse though you multiply gifts' tracks MT.
